bull.b: Sustained quarter-over-quarter LOQTORZI growth and rising new patient starts indicate an emerging, repeatable commercial revenue stream. Durable adoption and improved treatment duration can progressively reduce reliance on financing and support steady organic cash generation if reimbursement and physician uptake continue.

Consistent reductions in R&D and SG&A and explicit OpEx guidance show management discipline in allocating resources. A leaner cost base extends runway and increases optionality to fund priorities (commercial build, key readouts) without permanent dilution, improving long-term financial resilience.

Material reductions in secured/convertible debt and legacy liabilities materially improve capital structure and lower refinancing pressure. This structural de‑risking enhances flexibility to invest in core oncology assets and reduces the probability of near-term distress financing needs, strengthening long-term stability.

bear.b: A sharp quarter-over-quarter cash decline materially shortens runway and increases dependency on milestones, divestiture proceeds or external financing. Even with cost cuts, persistent negative operating cash flow makes the business sensitive to timing of commercial ramp and clinical readouts, raising structural funding risk.

bear.t: Deep ongoing losses and unstable revenue history
bear.b: Large cumulative losses and volatile revenue history signal limited operating leverage and constrained ability to self‑fund growth. Persistent negative margins erode equity and force recurring financing or asset sales, structurally increasing dilution risk and limiting long-term investment capacity.

Key value drivers depend on early, immature datasets and upcoming readouts. If data mature unfavorably or fail to translate to efficacy/regulatory outcomes, projected commercial and pipeline value could materially decline, making future revenue and financing prospects structurally uncertain.
